      Payload dictionaries
      
Dictionary values are substituted into the marked request. Use one dictionary for Sniper/Battering Ram, or multiple dictionaries for Pitchfork/Cluster Bomb. The generator is a shortcut for creating repetitive test values, not an automatic attack.

    The corpus is a finite set of checks taken from a published database. One click runs every one of them against the target: there is nothing to narrow and nothing to choose, so a run cannot quietly look at less than it says.
    
      
    
        
        
        
        
      
    
      
    
        
    
          
          
          
          
        
    
        
    
        
    
      
    
      
    
      
    
      
    #MethodPathStatusCheckEvidence
    
      
    
      
    
    
    

    
    
      
    The active scanner crawls the target, finds every injectable surface, probes it with nine detector modules, correlates the confirmed findings into attack chains, and attaches a proof to each one. A finding is rated only when its impact was demonstrated; everything else is marked unverified and capped below high.

    Scan options
        
    
          
          
          
          
          
          
          
          
        
    
        
    
          
          
        
    
        
    Both lists are yours and both are optional: an empty list means the run does not spend a single request on that probe. The parameter names are what the Target crawl read out of the application's own JavaScript — copy them from the Target panel — and the wordlist is a path dictionary.
    
        
    Every field is a number you chose: 0 for pages and delay means no bound, −1 for depth means follow links without a depth limit, and no value here reduces what the run can look at. The run stops when you cancel it or the target stops answering.
